faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.intro: If you have other questions, please reach out to us directly.

q1.question: Is the hair transplant procedure painful?
q1.answer: The procedure is performed under local anaesthesia. You may feel a brief discomfort while the anaesthesia is administered, but you do not feel pain during the operation. Mild tightness afterwards is normal and settles within a few days.

q2.question: When do hair transplant results become visible?
q2.answer: Transplanted hairs shed in the first 2–4 weeks — this is shock loss and is entirely normal. New hairs begin to emerge in months 3–4. The final result is visible at 12–18 months. Individual results may vary.

q3.question: How many grafts do I need?
q3.answer: The graft count depends on your hair-loss level, donor area capacity and personal expectations. A graft plan tailored to you is prepared during the free hair analysis.

q4.question: What is the difference between FUE and DHI?
q4.answer: With FUE, grafts are extracted one by one, channels are opened and the grafts are then placed. With DHI, the Choi pen extracts and implants the graft in a single step — improving angle and direction control. Which technique suits you is decided in the free consultation.

q5.question: I'm travelling from abroad — how does the process work?
q5.answer: Packages including airport transfers, hotel accommodation and clinic transport are available. A pre-assessment is carried out online, and a stay of two to three days in Istanbul is sufficient.

q6.question: When can I wash my hair normally again?
q6.answer: Gentle washing begins from day three. Once the grafts have settled, you can return to normal shower pressure and massage techniques from day fourteen. Avoid direct water pressure in the first week and pat dry with sterile gauze.

q7.question: Is shock loss normal — should I be worried?
q7.answer: Shock loss is entirely normal and is a sign of a healthy follicular cycle. The transplanted strands shed 2–4 weeks after the operation, but the living roots remain in place and continue to produce lasting, stronger hair. New growth typically begins around months 3–4.

q8.question: When can I return to intense exercise?
q8.answer: Light cardio can begin after 14 days. However, heavy lifting and contact sports should be avoided for 4 weeks — spikes in blood pressure can affect graft health. Return to your previous routine gradually.

q1.q: How many hairs does one graft contain?
q1.a: One graft (follicular unit) contains an average of 2–3 hairs. So 3,000 grafts equate to roughly 6,000–9,000 hairs. This ratio can vary with individual follicle structure.

q2.q: What is the maximum number of grafts in a single session?
q2.a: The safe upper limit is around 4,500–5,500 grafts. More than this can reduce graft survival rates. For larger needs, two sessions are recommended (6–12 months apart).

q3.q: Why is the donor area limited?
q3.a: Hair transplantation works on the principle of moving existing follicles from the genetically loss-resistant occipital area to the lost regions. New hair is not produced — it is redistributed. The lifetime harvestable graft count is around 8,000–10,000.

hero.title: FUE Hair Transplant:
hero.titleItalic: How It's Done, Outcomes and Realistic Expectations
hero.lede: FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction) is the most widely used hair transplant technique worldwide. Follicles are extracted from the donor area one by one with a fine micro-punch and implanted into thinning zones. Its scar-free design and large graft capacity make it effective even for advanced hair loss.

what.title: What is FUE?
what.p1: FUE stands for "Follicular Unit Extraction". Follicles in the donor area (typically the back and sides of the head) are extracted one at a time using micro-punches measuring 0.7–1.0 mm in diameter. This allows thousands of grafts to be harvested without a wide incision.
what.p2: While the harvested grafts rest in a special preservation solution, the surgeon opens micro-channels in the recipient zone. Grafts are placed into those channels following the natural growth direction; this delivers both a natural look and a lasting result.
what.p3: One of FUE's key advantages is that it leaves no linear scar in the donor area. The tiny dot-shaped marks from the micro-punch heal quickly and become invisible once the hair grows out.

how.title: How is FUE Performed?
how.lede: The procedure has five core stages. All steps are done under local anaesthesia; general anaesthesia is not required.

steps.title: Consultation and Planning
steps.body: Hair-loss severity is assessed (Norwood scale), graft count is calculated, and a natural hairline is designed. Donor density is reviewed to decide whether a single or multiple sessions are needed.

steps.title: Donor Area Preparation
steps.body: The donor area (typically nape and temples) is trimmed and local anaesthesia is administered. You may feel brief discomfort during the anaesthesia injection; no pain is felt during the procedure.

steps.title: Graft Extraction — with Micro-Punch
steps.body: A 0.7–1.0 mm micro-punch removes follicles one by one without harming surrounding tissue. Each graft can contain 1–4 hairs. Harvested grafts are kept in a special nourishing solution.

steps.title: Channel Opening and Placement
steps.body: The surgeon opens micro-channels in the recipient area following the natural growth direction and angle. Grafts are then placed into those channels one by one. This step directly determines the final look — experience is critical here.

steps.title: Recovery and Follow-up
steps.body: You go home the same day. The first 7–10 days are a sensitive care period. Crusting is normal and falls off by day 10. The first hairs emerge at month 3; final density is reached at month 12–18.

prosCons.title: Advantages and Limitations
prosCons.lede: FUE suits a wide range of patients, but it may not be ideal for every case. Here are its strengths and limits, transparently.

hero.title: DHI Hair Transplant:
hero.titleItalic: Choi Pen Technique, Advantages and Outcomes
hero.lede: DHI (Direct Hair Implantation) is the technique in which follicles are placed directly into the recipient area using a special implanter known as the Choi pen. The key difference from FUE is that channel opening and graft placement happen in a single step. The result is superior angle control and precise implantation among existing hair.

what.title: What is DHI?
what.p1: DHI stands for "Direct Hair Implantation". The Choi pen is at the heart of the method: each graft is loaded into this purpose-built implanter, and as the tip touches the skin, both a channel is opened and the graft is placed at the same time.
what.p2: This single-step process minimises the time grafts spend outside the body. More importantly, it increases the surgeon's control over angle, depth and direction. DHI offers a clear advantage in zones where implantation must happen between existing hair strands.
what.p3: Graft extraction uses the same method as FUE: each follicle is harvested individually with a micro-punch. The difference lies in how those grafts are then placed.
what.choiTitle: How Does the Choi Pen Work?
choiSteps: A single follicle (graft) is loaded into the Choi pen's tube.
The surgeon positions the pen on the skin at the desired angle and direction.
The trigger mechanism opens a channel and places the graft at the same time — both actions completed in one move.
The pen tube is cleaned, the next graft is loaded and the process repeats.

how.title: How is DHI Performed?
how.lede: The procedure is carried out in six stages. All steps are done under local anaesthesia; general anaesthesia is not required.

steps.title: Consultation and Planning
steps.body: Hair loss is evaluated, graft count is calculated, the hairline is designed. Whether DHI is the right technique for you is decided here.

steps.title: Local Anaesthesia
steps.body: Local anaesthesia is administered to both donor and recipient zones. You may feel brief discomfort during the injection; no pain is felt during the procedure thereafter.

steps.title: Graft Harvesting
steps.body: Follicles in the donor area are extracted one by one with a micro-punch. This step is identical to FUE. Harvested grafts are kept briefly in a special nourishing solution.

steps.title: Loading the Choi Pen and Direct Implantation
steps.body: Grafts are loaded one by one into the Choi pen's tube. The surgeon applies the pen to the skin at the planned angle and direction, completing channel opening and graft placement in a single move. This step distinguishes DHI from other techniques.

steps.title: Check and Dressing
steps.body: Once implantation is complete, both donor and recipient areas are inspected and dressings are applied. Verbal and written aftercare instructions are provided.

steps.title: Closure and Follow-up
steps.body: You go home the same day. A day-1 check-up is scheduled. Regular follow-up visits track healing and hair growth.

prosCons.title: Advantages and Limitations
prosCons.lede: DHI delivers superior outcomes for specific patient profiles, but it is not ideal in every case. Here are its strengths and limits, transparently.

pros.title: Superior Angle and Direction Control
pros.desc: The Choi pen places each graft at the desired angle and direction. Excellent harmony with the natural hair flow is achieved.

pros.title: Implantation Among Existing Hair

pros.title: High Density
pros.desc: Closer graft placement allows higher density per cm².

pros.title: Reduced Bleeding
pros.desc: With no pre-opened channels, bleeding in the recipient area is reduced.

pros.title: Shorter Out-of-Body Time
pros.desc: Direct implantation shortens the time grafts wait outside the body, which can favourably affect viability.

cons.title: Slower in Large Areas
cons.desc: Because the Choi pen requires loading one by one, DHI takes longer than FUE in wide zones requiring many grafts.

cons.title: More Expensive Than FUE
cons.desc: DHI is generally priced higher than FUE due to additional equipment cost and procedure time.

cons.title: Fewer Grafts per Session
cons.desc: Limited by loading time, DHI typically allows 2000–3500 grafts in a single session.

cons.title: Requires an Experienced Team
cons.desc: The Choi pen technique requires specialist training and experience. Outcome quality is directly tied to the team's competence.

items.a: In DHI, the Choi pen lets channel opening and graft placement happen in one step. In FUE, channels are opened first and grafts are placed afterwards. FUE, on the other hand, has the advantage of more grafts per session and shorter procedure time in wide areas.
Because DHI requires loading the Choi pen one graft at a time, it takes a little longer than FUE. A typical session is 5–7 hours. Time can vary with graft count and the scope of the procedure.

hero.title: Sapphire FUE:
hero.lede: Sapphire FUE is a variant of standard FUE performed with sapphire-crystal-tipped blades. The core principle is the same: the difference lies in the blade material used during channel opening. It can deliver smaller incisions, less tissue trauma and slightly faster recovery.

what.title: What is Sapphire FUE?
what.p1: Sapphire FUE is a variant of FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction) that uses sapphire-crystal-tipped blades instead of steel blades during channel opening. It is not a "new technique" — it is an enhancement of the existing FUE method.
what.p2: The core steps of the procedure are identical to standard FUE: graft harvesting from the donor area one by one, channel opening, and graft placement. The only difference is the blade material used in step three.
what.p3: Sapphire crystal belongs to the corundum family, the second-hardest mineral after diamond. This hardness keeps the blade tip sharper for longer and allows finer incisions.

diff.title: What Makes Sapphire Different?
diff.lede: It is important to know the truth about Sapphire FUE. We share its real advantages and limits openly.
diff.advantageIntro: Sapphire crystal is sharper than steel and creates a smoother incision surface. This means:
advantageItems: Smaller incision area — less tissue trauma
More precise channel opening — easier directional control
Faster recovery — 5–7 days (vs 7–10 days with standard FUE)
diff.limitsIntro: Per our honesty policy we must note:
limitsItems: There is no dramatic difference from standard FUE — the core principle is the same
What determines the final result is not the blade material but the surgeon's experience
There may be a cost difference — sapphire-tipped blades are more expensive
Graft survival rate is similar with both methods
diff.limitsFooter: Some clinics market Sapphire FUE as "next-generation technology". In reality, only the blade material differs. It is important you know this.

how.title: How is Sapphire FUE Performed?
how.lede: The procedure steps are identical to standard FUE. The only difference is in step 3 (channel opening), where sapphire-tipped blades are used.

step1.title: Consultation and Planning
step1.body: Hair-loss assessment, graft count calculation, hairline design. Whether Sapphire FUE is right for you is decided here. The most appropriate technique for each patient is selected through individual evaluation.

step2.title: Graft Harvesting (Same)
step2.body: Local anaesthesia is administered. Follicles are harvested one by one from the donor area (typically the nape) with a micro-punch. This step is exactly the same as standard FUE. Harvested grafts are kept in a special solution.

step3.title: Channel Opening — Sapphire Blade
step3.body: The micro-channels for graft placement are opened with sapphire-crystal-tipped blades instead of steel. The sharper, smoother sapphire tip enables smaller channel openings. Channel angle, depth and direction are precisely set by the surgeon.

step4.title: Graft Placement (Same)
step4.body: Harvested grafts are placed one by one into the opened channels. This step is the same as standard FUE. The procedure totals 4–6 hours. You go home the same day.

items.q: What is the difference between Sapphire FUE and regular FUE?
items.a: The core difference is the blade material. In Sapphire FUE, sapphire-crystal-tipped blades replace steel blades during channel opening, allowing smaller and more precise incisions. The fundamental steps — graft harvesting, channel opening and placement — are identical to standard FUE. It is not "a completely different technique" but a variant of FUE.

The same local anaesthesia is used in both techniques; you do not feel pain during the procedure. Recovery discomfort may be slightly less because the sapphire blade creates smaller incisions. The intra-operative experience is virtually the same in both methods. "Painless procedure" is not medically accurate — brief discomfort during anaesthesia injection is possible.

Because sapphire-tipped blades cost more than steel blades, Sapphire FUE may be priced slightly higher than standard FUE. The difference varies by clinic. Our free consultation provides a personalised assessment and price tailored to your hair-loss situation.

items.q: Are results better than standard FUE?
items.a: Sapphire FUE may offer a slight advantage in recovery time. However, the final result — density, naturalness and durability — depends largely on the surgeon's experience, technical skill, and your post-op compliance. Blade material alone is not the determining factor. Standard FUE performed by an experienced surgeon may yield better outcomes than Sapphire FUE performed by an inexperienced one.

hero.title: Beard Transplant Istanbul
hero.lede: A beard transplant is a permanent restoration procedure that moves follicles from the donor area at the back of the neck to the face — chin, cheeks, or moustache zones — using microsurgical methods. With DHI's precise angle control, a full appearance aligned with the natural growth direction is achieved.

shortAnswer.title: Short answer
shortAnswer.body: A beard transplant is a permanent microsurgical procedure that thickens sparse, patchy or gappy beards using follicles harvested from the nape. With the DHI Choi pen, each graft is placed at 30–45 degrees flat — the natural beard growth angle. The procedure takes 3–5 hours under local anaesthesia. Most patients receive between 1,500–2,500 grafts. Final results appear at 10–12 months.

hero.title: Eyebrow Transplant Istanbul
hero.lede: An eyebrow transplant is a precise microsurgical procedure that restores brows that are naturally sparse, thinned by over-plucking, or lost after trauma or burns, using single-hair grafts. The most critical detail: each graft is placed at a 10–15 degree flat angle — the natural growth direction of brow hair.

shortAnswer.title: Short answer
shortAnswer.body: An eyebrow transplant is a permanent procedure where single-hair grafts harvested from the nape are placed in the brow area using a combination of FUE+DHI. Its most critical feature is angle control: a 10–15° flat angle. The procedure takes 2–3 hours. A full pair uses 300–500 grafts; symmetry correction uses 150–300 grafts. Final results appear at 8–12 months.

candidates.title: Who Is a Suitable Candidate?
careful: Skin disease in the face area

angle.title: Why is the angle so critical?
angle.p1: Brow hair naturally grows at a 10–15 degree flat angle to the skin surface. This angle gives the brow its natural "laid-down" appearance.
angle.p2: If grafts are placed vertically or at 30°+, the new hair looks like vertical scalp hair — a completely unnatural result.
angle.p3: Eyebrow transplants therefore require greater angle precision and experience than beard or scalp transplants.

how.title: How is an Eyebrow Transplant Performed?

steps.title: Brow Design
steps.text: Facial anatomy, inter-eye distance and personal preference are considered. Symmetry and natural arch are drawn with a pencil. The design is approved by the patient.

steps.title: Local Anaesthesia
steps.text: Local anaesthesia is administered to both donor (nape) and recipient (brow) zones. The anaesthesia process is short due to the small area.

steps.title: Single-Hair Graft Harvesting
steps.text: Single-hair follicular units are selected and harvested from the nape with a micro-punch. Multi-hair grafts are not used for the brow — critical for a natural look.

steps.title: Precise Placement
steps.text: Each graft is placed at a 10–15° flat angle aligned with the brow's natural growth direction, in a specific sequence. Microscope assistance ensures precision.

steps.title: Check and Closure
steps.text: Each hair direction is checked individually. Symmetry is compared. Aside from very mild redness, there are no visible signs of healing.

trim.title: Important: implanted brows need trimming
trim.body: Because implanted hairs come from the nape, they keep growing like scalp hair. In the early period, trimming 1–2 times per week is required. Over time, the hairs adapt to the brow rhythm and the trimming frequency decreases — but it does not stop entirely. This is a different aftercare requirement from a scalp transplant.

absolute.title: In which medical conditions is it not performed?

items.title: Active Alopecia Areata

items.title: Insufficient Donor Area
items.desc: If enough grafts cannot be harvested, the result will not be satisfactory. Donor capacity is measured during consultation.

items.title: Bleeding Disorder
items.desc: Bleeding risk increases and wound healing is impaired. Patients on anticoagulants require special evaluation.

items.title: Active Skin Diseases
items.desc: If active lesions such as psoriasis or eczema are present in the recipient or donor area, the procedure cannot be performed.

items.title: Uncontrolled Chronic Illness
items.desc: Uncontrolled diabetes, heart disease or immune issues can endanger the recovery process.

items.title: Certain Cancer Treatments
items.desc: During chemotherapy, the chance of graft survival is very low. Reassessment after treatment completion is possible.

items.title: Unrealistic Expectations
items.desc: To prevent disappointment, sound expectation management is essential. The consultation includes this assessment.

items.title: Under 18
items.desc: The hair-loss pattern has not yet stabilised. Early implantation may produce results that need correction later.

relative.title: In which situations is careful evaluation needed?

items.title: Controlled Diabetes
items.desc: If blood sugar is well controlled and you have a doctor's clearance, individual evaluation may be possible. Wound healing is monitored closely.

items.title: Young Age (18–24)

items.q: Who is not suitable for a hair transplant?
items.a: Active alopecia areata, insufficient donor area, age under 18, uncontrolled chronic illnesses (diabetes, heart disease), bleeding disorders, active skin diseases, and individuals with unrealistic expectations may not be suitable for a hair transplant. The final decision is made by a specialist.

items.q: Is there an age limit for a hair transplant?
items.a: It is not performed under age 18 because the loss pattern is not yet stable. Age 25+ is generally considered the ideal starting point. There is no upper limit; donor capacity and general health are decisive.

items.q: Can people with diabetes have a hair transplant?
items.a: Patients with controlled diabetes, with a doctor's clearance and appropriate blood-sugar levels, may be evaluated. Uncontrolled diabetes adversely affects wound healing and may make a hair transplant unsuitable.

items.q: Can women have a hair transplant?
items.a: Yes. Women with Ludwig-pattern thinning or hair loss after trauma or burns can be suitable candidates. In diffuse loss, the underlying cause should be identified and treated first.

items.q: Can people with alopecia areata have a hair transplant?
items.a: A hair transplant is not advised in active alopecia areata, since the autoimmune reaction can also affect the implanted grafts. In long-term stable cases, individual evaluation may be possible.
